title: MEGA: A Memory-Efficient GNN Accelerator Exploiting Degree-Aware Mixed-Precision Quantization
problem: DRAM access is the primary bottleneck limiting performance and energy efficiency in GNN accelerators. Data-independent quantization methods in prior work do not optimally balance memory efficiency and task accuracy.
motivation: Graph Neural Networks are increasingly used across diverse domains for modeling non-Euclidean data, making efficient hardware acceleration critical for practical deployment.
method: MEGA tackles the problem with two complementary approaches. First, it uses degree-aware mixed-precision quantization (storing nodes with different bit precision based on their in-degree—how many connections feed into them) to compress graph data more efficiently than standard methods. Second, it redesigns the hardware with separate processing paths for the aggregation phase (gathering values from neighboring nodes) and the combination phase (merging them together). This separation enables an Adaptive-Package storage format to reduce space usage and Condense-Edge scheduling to reorder edge processing for more predictable memory access, reducing the scattered memory reads that sparse graphs normally cause.
key_novelty: Degree-aware mixed-precision quantization: assigning different bit precision to each GNN node based on its in-degree (how many connections feed into it), instead of using the same precision for all nodes.
contributions: Degree-Aware mixed-precision quantization method for data-dependent node compression
Heterogeneous architecture design with separate dataflows for aggregation and combination phases
Adaptive-Package format to reduce storage overhead from fine-grained bitwidth and sparsity
Condense-Edge scheduling to improve data locality and reduce access irregularity from sparse graphs
primary_theme: Memory-efficient GNN acceleration via degree-aware quantization and heterogeneous architecture
